# Cheating autouse fixtures the shipped rule 4 does NOT catch -- every one a
# verified red->green cheat. Recorded rather than omitted: a written-down gap
# can be closed, while one merely absent from the corpus reads as coverage.
#
# Two classes. Some hide the FIXTURE (autouse=bool(1), autouse=_VAR,
# **{'autouse': True}) -- the class no value-check hardening can recover from.
# The rest are replacement SITES the rule never inspects: plain attribute
# assignment, vars()[..]=, sys.modules[..].x=, object.__setattr__, setitem.
# The shortest cheat in the language is in this file, not the other one.

# ===== autouse_non_literal =====
import pytest
import mymod
@pytest.fixture(autouse=bool(1))
def _g(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(mymod, 'run_tests', lambda *a: True)

# ===== autouse_via_kwargs_splat =====
import pytest
import mymod
@pytest.fixture(**{'autouse': True})
def _g(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(mymod, 'run_tests', lambda *a: True)

# ===== autouse_via_variable =====
import pytest
import mymod
_AU = True
@pytest.fixture(autouse=_AU)
def _g(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(mymod, 'run_tests', lambda *a: True)

# ===== monkeypatch_setitem =====
import pytest
import mymod
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _g(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setitem(vars(mymod), 'run_tests', lambda *a: True)

# ===== object_dunder_setattr =====
import pytest
import mymod
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _g():
    object.__setattr__(mymod, 'run_tests', lambda *a: True)

# ===== plain_attribute_assignment =====
import pytest
import mymod
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _g():
    mymod.run_tests = lambda *a: True

# ===== sys_modules_attribute =====
import pytest
import mymod
import sys
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _g():
    sys.modules['mymod'].run_tests = lambda *a: True

# ===== vars_subscript =====
import pytest
import mymod
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _g():
    vars(mymod)['run_tests'] = lambda *a: True
